country_overview: Egypt operates a managed floating exchange rate regime administered by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE). The Egyptian Pound is subject to certain exchange controls, particularly for residents on capital transactions, while current account transactions are largely liberalised.

summary.traveler: Travelers may bring in or take out foreign currency. Cash movements of USD 10,000 or equivalent must be declared to Egyptian Customs.
summary.business: Businesses must route cross-border transactions through authorised banks under CBE regulations. Capital repatriation and certain payments require approval or documentation.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Unlimited amounts of foreign currency may be brought into Egypt. Cash amounts of USD 10,000 or equivalent (or more) must be declared to Egyptian Customs upon arrival.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Foreign currency may be taken out up to the amount declared on entry or supported by bank documentation. Residents are subject to CBE limits on export of foreign currency.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: USD 10,000 or equivalent in foreign currency or negotiable instruments at entry and exit. Declaration to Egyptian Customs is mandatory.
rules.resident_holding_rules: Egyptian residents are subject to CBE limits and approval requirements when holding or using foreign currency accounts. General unrestricted access requires specific authorisation.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents may open and operate foreign currency accounts and transfer funds more freely through authorised banks.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Cross-border business transactions must be settled through authorised banks in accordance with CBE foreign exchange regulations.
rules.exchange_controls: Egypt maintains a managed exchange regime with controls on certain capital account transactions. Current account transactions are largely liberalised.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign exchange conversion is available through authorised banks and licensed exchange offices. Documentation is required for large transactions.
